title: Devcontainer: pinned agent toolchain and hook wiring
summary: This change turns the devcontainer image from a Rust-only build box into a fully pinned factory workbench. It adds moon, Node 22 + pnpm, Bun, gh, actionlint, uv, the NVIDIA skill linters, and four coding agents (codex, claude-code, opencode, omp) at exact versions with published SHA-256 checks, builds the dsh/omp/opencode writing-check plugins from the workspace lockfile, and installs every agent's hook files root-owned and read-only so `osf hook` fires on prompt and stop. The git wrapper stops relying on a system-wide core.hooksPath and instead forces /opt/factory/githooks on the command line for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, and a battery of build-time tests proves the wrapper's refusals, the hook wiring, the read-only toolchain, and a clean image.

nodes.label: Developer
nodes.summary: The person editing the repository and running the container.

nodes.label: Workspace mount
nodes.subtitle: /workspace
nodes.summary: devcontainer.json now binds the host repository at /workspace and sets workspaceFolder, so the wrapper and the mount agree on one path.

nodes.label: dev user
nodes.summary: The non-root container user, with no password-less root access and no sudo group membership.

nodes.label: osf-path.sh
nodes.subtitle: /etc/profile.d
nodes.summary: A login shell resets PATH before reading /etc/profile.d, which would drop osf, cargo and every agent binary; this script puts them back.

nodes.label: devcontainer.json
nodes.summary: Adds the workspace mount, forwards GH_TOKEN from the host, and extends postCreateCommand to check moon, node and pnpm as well as osf.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.subtitle: +493 lines
nodes.summary: The image definition: every tool below is fetched from its own release, checked against a published SHA-256, and installed root-owned.

nodes.label: moon
nodes.summary: The task runner every factory check goes through. Moved from /opt/factory/bin to /usr/local/bin and now installed before the osf build.

nodes.label: Node 22 + pnpm
nodes.summary: Node from the official nodejs.org tarball and pnpm enabled through corepack, so the pnpm version always matches the repo's packageManager field.

nodes.label: Bun
nodes.summary: omp's bin/cli.js has a bun shebang, so omp needs Bun rather than plain Node.

nodes.label: gh + actionlint
nodes.summary: Builder-role tools: gh for opening and checking pull requests, actionlint for the writing-a-workflow skill and this project's own CI.

nodes.label: uv + skill linters
nodes.subtitle: SkillSpector, SkillEvaluator
nodes.summary: uv installs the two NVIDIA skill-checking tools at pinned commits, with UV_TOOL_DIR and UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR moved out from under root's home so dev can read them.

nodes.label: Rust toolchain
nodes.subtitle: rustfmt + clippy
nodes.summary: rustfmt and clippy are added to the base image's pinned toolchain before the write bits are stripped from /usr/local/cargo and /usr/local/rustup.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/osf
nodes.summary: Built from this workspace and installed root-owned and read-only. The build now uses cargo registry and git cache mounts.

nodes.label: git wrapper
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/git
nodes.summary: Refuses --no-verify and -n on commit and --no-verify on push, then calls the real git. Now forces core.hooksPath on the command line for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT instead of relying on a system-wide setting.

nodes.label: git hooks
nodes.subtitle: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push
nodes.summary: Root-owned, read-only hook files that each only call osf.

nodes.label: osf hook
nodes.subtitle: prompt, stop
nodes.summary: The one osf subcommand every agent's hook file calls. It supports a prompt event and a stop event, and no pre-tool-use event.

nodes.label: codex
nodes.summary: Installed as a global npm package. Its hook files live at real system paths under /etc/codex, and only the prompt event is wired because its HookEventName enum has no turn-end event.

nodes.label: claude-code
nodes.summary: Installed as a global npm package. Its settings.json is written under the dev home and copied to /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json so a changed HOME cannot move it.

nodes.label: opencode
nodes.summary: Installed as opencode-ai, the package its own plugin SDK matches. Its config is copied to /etc/opencode/opencode.json, and its plugin is installed under the dev home's node_modules.

nodes.label: omp
nodes.summary: Installed as a global npm package and run on Bun. It has no system-wide hook location, so its hook file stays under the dev home only.

nodes.label: dsh
nodes.subtitle: 0.2.0-rc.2
nodes.summary: Installed from its own lockfile at /opt/dsh. Its factory and headless profiles each carry the osf writing-check plugin, with only cordis.yml left dev-owned because dsh rewrites it on every start.

nodes.label: plugin build
nodes.subtitle: pnpm --filter
nodes.summary: Builds the dsh, omp and opencode integrations from the workspace lockfile so their dependency versions match what pnpm -r test already proves.

nodes.label: build-time tests
nodes.subtitle: 8 scripts
nodes.summary: git-wrapper, git-hooks, agent-hooks, coding-agent-tools, builder-tools, dsh-starts, skills-installed, toolchain-readonly and image-clean all run during the build, so a broken wrapper or hook fails the build instead of shipping quietly.

nodes.label: devcontainer-image.yml
nodes.subtitle: GitHub Actions
nodes.summary: A new workflow that builds the devcontainer image in CI.

edges.label: prompt event
edges.summary: Codex's /etc/codex/hooks/osf-prompt.toml calls osf hook on the prompt event; its HookEventName enum has no turn-end event, so no stop hook is wired.

edges.label: UserPromptSubmit
edges.summary: The managed settings file wires UserPromptSubmit to osf hook prompt, the same command the repository's own .claude/hooks.json names.

edges.label: Claude-format bridge
edges.summary: Each dsh profile registers the Claude-format hooks bridge pointed at this repository's own .claude/hooks.json.

edges.label: core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
edges.summary: The wrapper now passes the hooks path on the command line for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, so a scratch repository under /tmp is not affected the way a system-wide setting would be.

flows.title: A coding agent's prompt reaches osf hook
flows.summary: Every agent the image installs fires the same osf hook command on the prompt event, through a hook file that is root-owned and read-only. The path from the agent to osf differs per agent: codex reads a system file under /etc/codex, claude-code reads a managed settings file, and dsh bridges through the repository's own .claude/hooks.json.

messages.label: reads /etc/codex/hooks/osf-prompt.toml
messages.note: Root-owned and mode 0444, so the agent cannot rewrite its own hook.

messages.label: Claude-format hooks bridge
messages.note: The bridge is pointed at this repository's own .claude/hooks.json rather than a file under the root-owned profile directory.

flows.title: A commit under the workspace goes through the wrapper
flows.summary: The wrapper refuses the flags that would skip the hooks, then forces the hooks path on the command line for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT. The hook then calls osf, which is the same binary the agents' hook files call.

messages.label: refuse --no-verify and -n
messages.note: The refusal is what the build-time git-wrapper test proves.

messages.label: core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
messages.note: Forced on the command line only for repositories under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT, so a scratch repository under /tmp keeps its own hooks.
